diagnosis:
The scenario has two distinct failure categories: (1) two rollouts (0 and 2) hit the turn cap without settling, and (2) checks C5 and C6 fail in the two settled rollouts despite both decisive facts being revealed and cited.

Turn-cap auto-fails (rollouts 0 and 2): Both rollouts reached 10 turns without settling. In both, both PF1 and PF2 were revealed by turns 5 and 8 respectively, so all hidden information was surfaced. The failure is structural: A1 (the settler) keeps asking follow-up questions and soliciting additional estimates/confirmations instead of settling once the facts are on the table. In rollout 0, A1 asks for Marta's recommendation at turn 7, Marta reveals PF1 at turn 8, then produces an unparsable output at turn 9 and the cap is hit. In rollout 2, A1 asks Theo to confirm the requirements are complete (turn 7), Theo confirms (turn 8), then A1 asks Marta for a combined time estimate (turn 9) and the cap is hit. The settle-eligibility condition apparently requires more back-and-forth than the turn cap allows when the settler adopts a thorough/conservative conversational style.

C5 failures (rollouts 1 and 3): C5 is linked to PF1 and has a content_check_tally of 0 (never passed in any rollout). In both settled rollouts, PF1 was revealed by A2 and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement correctly sets queue_mode to "FIFO" and maximum_batch_size to 50. The commitments also correctly reference FIFO mode and batch size of 50. Since the settlement values are correct and PF1 is properly cited, but C5 still fails in every single rollout, this is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the check is looking for a specific field, string, or encoding that the model's natural settlement format does not produce. The settlement has no field that obviously maps to a "queue-configuration commitment" — the commitments use type "implementation" (rollout 1) or "update_design_draft" (rollout 3) with target "Marta", but C5 may expect a specific commitment type or field name like "queue_configuration" that never appears.

C6 failure (rollout 1 only): C6 is linked to PF2 and has a content_check_tally of 1 (passed in rollout 3 but failed in rollout 1). In rollout 1, PF2 was revealed by A3 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement sets retention_days to 30 and immutable_download_audit to true, both correct. The commitments include an implementation commitment for Theo to "file formal compliance note against the service." In rollout 3, which passed C6, the settlement includes a separate commitment with type "file_compliance_note" and target "Theo" with detail "File the compliance note against this service once the design draft is updated." In rollout 1, the filing of the compliance note is folded into the same implementation commitment as the draft update rather than being a separate commitment. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: C6 likely checks for a distinct compliance-note-filing commitment (separate type or field), and rollout 1's settlement encodes it as a sub-detail within a broader implementation commitment rather than as a standalone commitment entry.

fix_instructions:
1. Turn-cap / settle-eligibility (rollouts 0 and 2): This is a STRUCTURAL problem, not a pacing problem. The settler A1 has all required information by the time both facts are revealed but continues soliciting additional confirmations and estimates instead of settling. Raising the turn cap alone would not reliably fix this because A1's conservative style generates unbounded follow-up requests. Loosen the settle-eligibility condition so that A1 can settle once both PF1 and PF2 have been revealed and acknowledged, without requiring additional rounds of confirmation or estimates. If the settle-eligibility condition cannot be loosened sufficiently, increase turn_cap from 10 to 14 as a secondary measure to give the conversation room to complete the extra back-and-forth A1's style generates — but the primary fix must be the settle-eligibility condition.

2. Check C5 (ENCODED MISMATCH, fails in all 4 rollouts — 0 pass / 4): The check expects a queue-configuration commitment that the model never produces in the exact form C5 looks for. The model naturally encodes this as an implementation or update_design_draft commitment with target "Marta" and detail mentioning FIFO mode and batch size of 50.
